note: The #claims temp table holds the filtered claims with accident_year and the normalised lob_code. In Spark it becomes an intermediate DataFrame.
snippet:
IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#claims') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #claims;

        SELECT c.claim_id,
               c.loss_date,
               YEAR(c.loss_date)        AS accident_year,
               UPPER(RTRIM(c.lob_code)) AS lob_code
        INTO   #claims

note: The #paid temp table holds the payments joined to claims, with their dev_year. In Spark it becomes an intermediate DataFrame.
snippet:
IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#paid') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #paid;

        SELECT cl.claim_id,
               p.payment_id,
               cl.accident_year,
               cl.lob_code,
               DATEDIFF(YEAR, cl.loss_date, p.payment_date) AS dev_year,
               p.amount
        INTO   #paid

note: dev_year counts the calendar-year boundaries crossed between loss_date and payment_date, not the full years elapsed. A loss on 2023-12-31 paid on 2024-01-01 lands in dev_1. Spark needs year(payment_date) - year(loss_date), not months_between or a day-based calculation.
The #tri temp table holds the pivoted triangle before the insert. In Spark it becomes an intermediate DataFrame.
snippet:
IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#tri') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #tri;

        SELECT pv.accident_year,
               pv.lob_code,
               pv.[0] AS d0, pv.[1] AS d1, pv.[2] AS d2, pv.[3] AS d3,
               pv.[4] AS d4, pv.[5] AS d5, pv.[6] AS d6
        INTO   #tri

note: The PIVOT implicitly groups by accident_year and lob_code and keeps only dev_year 0-6, so payments in dev years above 6 are dropped. Spark needs groupBy('accident_year','lob_code').pivot('dev_year',[0..6]).sum('amount') with the values listed, and missing cells stay NULL.
